Need to answer "why" in your commit message.

FWIW, the sd-bus version of these have been exposed for some time (but weren't available when this code was written).  I would much rather see we transition to those than try to continue changing something that shouldn't exist in the first place.  Is that something you're interested in?

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/26b2085d54ebbfca8637362eafcb4a8e3faf832f/src/systemd/sd-bus.h#L34

> Need to answer "why" in your commit message.

to avoid code duplication, see

https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#es3-dont-repeat-yourself-avoid-redundant-code

>  I would much rather see we transition to those

I am sorry, i don't get it, you linked to functions 

```
int sd_bus_interface_name_is_valid(const char *p);
int sd_bus_service_name_is_valid(const char *p);
int sd_bus_member_name_is_valid(const char *p);
int sd_bus_object_path_is_valid(const char *p);
```

and from what i could gather these do not lead to any regex.
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5366dbdbd44ba4dc0c914dd4daa1a5297e0b2bde/src/libsystemd/sd-bus/bus-internal.c#L119

Instead they are implemented in a simple loop.

EM cannot just validate object paths and member names, it must also sanitize them.

But that's out of scope for this patch, right? This patch is a simple change to deduplicate regex definitions.
Marking as resolved since there was no further response in around 2 months. Please re-open in case you want to answer my questions.

> to avoid code duplication, see

You were asked to put it in your commit message.  That's great you quoted CPP core guidelines, which isn't really necessary.  The point is that this commit message says "what" you did, which I can see from the diff, it doesn't say why you did it.

> and from what i could gather these do not lead to any regex.

Correct, they implement a "correct" parser not based on a regex.  I didn't realize these were used in regex_replace, so yes, they wouldn't be appropriate, but sdbusplus::message::object_path would be the right thing to use here.

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/sd_bus_path_encode.3.html

Would be the "dry" version of this if that's the goal we're chasing, but at the same time there's a lot of history here:
https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/issues/60

I don't understand what's so hard about this change. We are going in circles for months here. I think the change is good as-is.

If you prefer a different commit message, please upload the next patch revision and write it down. Let's not scope creep into trying to fix broken D-Bus encoding schemes.

Otherwise if you prefer to keep various copies of these regex definitions around, who am i to tell you different.
Please mark WIP until this is tested.  This isn't a trivial refactor

The next change in the relation chain has a manual test
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/85783

I am trying to understand what is complicated about this change. There is

- 2 regexes
- 1 type: `std::regex`
- 1 function: `std::regex_replace`

Since the type, functions, and regexes all stay the same, what has effectively changed?

We will get the same overload of the same function, with the same type and same regex value, right?
Change is tested in the next patch. Marking as resolved since it's been almost 2 months without any response from your side.

Haven't really reviewed code yet.  See proposal below, if that doesn't track, and you'd rather continue with this type of refactor, that's fine, but I suspect the transition to sd-bus.h would be better for both of us.

```suggestion
Refactor dbus regexes

```
